account: Karthik Muralidharan and Abhijeet Singh evaluated Mindspark, the personalized adaptive learning software of Educational Initiatives, in government Adarsh schools in four districts of Rajasthan, India, with the Government of Rajasthan. They randomly assigned 80 schools with about 6,500 students. The 40 treatment schools received a Mindspark computer lab and a local lab assistant, and they replaced about a quarter of weekly math and Hindi time in primary grades, and 40 to 50 percent in middle grades, with lab periods on the software. The other 40 schools continued regular teaching. Baseline tests took place in October 2017. After 18 months, students in treatment schools scored 0.22 standard deviations higher in math and 0.20 standard deviations higher in Hindi on independently designed tests. The authors describe this as a 50 to 66 percent increase in the productivity of school time. Gains did not vary by gender, socioeconomic status or initial scores. The program had no effect on school exam scores. The estimate covers the whole program, including the computers and the lab assistants. The paper is an NBER working paper revised in November 2025.

ai_role.statement: Schools were randomized to the whole program or to regular teaching. The program bundled the adaptive software with new computer labs, lab assistants and changed timetables, so the trial does not separate the software's adaptation from the extra equipment and time on computers.
